{{Field procedure|summary=Break surface deposits from asteroids with an abrasion blaster and collect the resulting materials or commodities.}}

Use this procedure for [[Surface Deposit Mining|surface deposit mining]], including the post-detonation cleanup stage of [[Core Mining|core mining]].

{{Draft warning}}

== Required equipment ==

* [[Abrasion Blaster]]
* [[Collector Limpet Controller]]
* [[Refinery]]
* Limpets and cargo space
* Optional: [[Prospector Limpet Controller]] and [[Pulse Wave Analyser]] when searching for suitable asteroids

== Procedure ==

{{Procedure steps|
# Identify an asteroid with visible surface deposits, or inspect a cracked core asteroid after detonation.
# Target a visible deposit.
# Fire the abrasion blaster until the deposit breaks free.
# Keep collector limpets active so the released material is recovered.
# Check the refinery and cargo hold before moving to the next deposit.
# Repeat until no useful deposits remain or the run plan changes.
}}

== Completion check ==

The asteroid is complete when useful visible deposits have been dislodged and collected, or when the remaining deposits are not worth the time, cargo, or refinery space for the run.

== Common problems ==

* '''Deposit will not break free:''' confirm that the visible deposit is targeted and that the abrasion blaster is hitting it directly.
* '''Collectors keep dying:''' back away from jagged asteroid surfaces and avoid dragging limpets through rock.
* '''Cargo does not appear:''' check refinery bins; fragments may still be processing or blocked.
* '''No visible deposits after a core blast:''' inspect the cracked pieces before leaving, but do not assume every angle has a recoverable target.
